ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graphs of the linear function $y_{1}=mx\ (m\ne 0)$ and $y_{2}=x+3$ intersect at point $A(-1, 2)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $mx>x+3$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Since $mx > x + 3$, \\
it follows that $y_1 > y_2$, \\
thus $x < -1$. \\
Hence, the answer is $\boxed{x < -1}$.

method.method_draft: Use an algebraic computation supported by the diagram. First describe the figure: the line y1=mx is the line through the origin with negative slope, and it intersects the upward line y2=x+3 at A. From the text, A=(-1,2) lies on y1=mx. Substitute A into y1=mx: 2=m(-1), so m=-2. Then solve the target inequality mx>x+3 as -2x>x+3. Rearranging gives -3x>3; dividing by the negative number -3 reverses the inequality, giving x<-1.
